title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance for Evaluation of Long-Term Outcome
summary: This study investigates whether certain findings in cardiac magnetic resonance imaging are associated with long-term risk of cardiovascular disease and death. Existing data from patients examined at Heidelberg University Hospital between 2005 and 2007 will be analyzed. In addition, an existing cohort of healthy participants from the Heidelberg site of the Healthy Hearts Consortium will be used as a comparison group. Information on later health events will be obtained from official registries and medical records. The aim is to better understand which changes in the heart are linked to increased health risks.
conditions: Ischemic heart disease, non-ischemic cardiomyopathies, inflammatory heart diseases and structural heart diseases including subclinical myocardial alterations

interventions.name: This is a retrospective, non-randomized observational study. Patients who underwent cardiac magnetic resonance imaging at Heidelberg University Hospital between 2005 and 2007 are included. Demographic, clinical, and imaging data are obtained from digital health records and the PACS system and stored

In addition to the patient cohort, an existing cohort of healthy participants from the Heidelberg site of the Healthy Hearts Consortium (n = 192) will be used as a control group and re-analyzed using a harmonized analysis pipeline identical to the patient cohort.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who underwent cardiac magnetic resonance imaging at Heidelberg University Hospital between 2005 and 2007 are eligible for inclusion. Availability of relevant imaging datasets and baseline clinical data at the time of examination is required. In addition, availability of follow-up data must be ensured.
In addition, healthy participants from the Heidelberg site of the Healthy Hearts Consortium are included as a control group.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients are excluded in case of incomplete datasets, particularly when essential imaging or clinical information is missing. Furthermore, cases without available follow-up data and examinations with insufficient image quality precluding reliable analysis are excluded.
